readerTitle: Two small changes to a pricing page that nobody reads closely
caseNote: 가상 사례 (대형 은행 안의 앱 팀, 화물 운송 회사) · 모든 수치는 설명용 · 개념 근거는 앵커링·디코이 연구
insight: 가격표를 바꿀 때는 가격을 내리기보다 고객이 무엇과 비교하게 될지를 먼저 설계한다.
misconception: 상위 플랜 가입을 늘리려면 상위 플랜 가격을 내려야 한다.

sources.text: Tversky, A. & Kahneman, D. (1974). Judgment under Uncertainty: Heuristics and Biases. Science.
Huber, J., Payne, J. W. & Puto, C. (1982). Adding Asymmetrically Dominated Alternatives. Journal of Consumer Research.
앱 팀과 운송 회사 사례, 모든 가격과 가입 비율은 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: 모든 수치는 설명용 가상 수치입니다. 계산 확인: Pro $39 − Starter Plus $35 = $4. Starter Plus(리마인더 20건)가 Pro(무제한 리마인더 + 은행 거래 연동)보다 $4만 싸고 기능은 명확히 적어 비대칭 열위(디코이) 조건을 만족합니다.
운송 사례: Economy 7일 $400, Priority 4일 $650, Express 2일 $1,200, Standard 5일 $630, Saver 10일 $300. Standard는 Priority보다 $20 싸고 하루 느려 Priority를 돋보이게 하는 디코이 역할입니다. 모두 가상 수치입니다.
앵커링·디코이 효과의 크기는 상황마다 다르며, 신중히 비교하는 B2B 구매자에게는 약할 수 있다는 점을 Watch out 카드에 반영했습니다. 특정 효과 크기 수치는 인용하지 않았습니다.

cards.title: Two small changes to a pricing page that nobody reads closely
body: A team of four inside a large regional bank runs an invoicing app for small-business clients. The pricing page shows two plans: Starter at $15 a month and Pro at $39.
Nine in ten sign-ups pick Starter. Yet Pro includes automatic payment reminders, the feature late-paid business owners need most. The team's boss wants more Pro sign-ups, without cutting any price.

image.label: A simple two-plan pricing page on a laptop
image.brief: 노트북 화면에 단순한 요금제 페이지. 왼쪽 "Starter $15" 카드에 사람 아이콘이 잔뜩 몰려 있고, 오른쪽 "Pro $39" 카드는 한산함. 실제 은행이나 앱 로고는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: What do you change first?
body: Some clients have staff and an outside accountant. They have asked for multi-user access, which the team could offer as a real plan.
Which first move best lifts Pro sign-ups?

options.text: Cut Pro to $29 so the gap with Starter looks smaller
options.feedback: You may win some sign-ups, but you give up $10 on every Pro client. The page still asks people to compare Pro with a cheaper plan.

options.text: Add a real $99 Business plan with multi-user access, shown first
options.feedback: This is **anchoring**: the first big number becomes the reference point. Next to $99, $39 reads as the sensible middle, and some firms will buy Business too.

options.text: Put a "Most popular" badge on Pro
options.feedback: A badge can nudge, and it's cheap to try. But Pro is still the most expensive plan in view, so the reference point hasn't moved.

cards.title: The first number sets the scale.
body: People judge prices by comparison. The first price they see tends to become the yardstick for the rest.
With only Starter and Pro, $39 was "the expensive one." With Business at $99 shown first, $39 becomes the middle option. Nothing about Pro changed. Its neighbours did.
The anchor must be a plan someone would really buy. Here, firms with staff need it, so it earns money on its own.

image.label: Price scale moving as a $99 plan appears
image.brief: 가로 눈금자 두 개 비교. 위쪽 눈금은 $15~$39로 짧고 $39가 끝에 있어 "expensive"로 표시. 아래쪽 눈금은 $15~$99로 길고 $39가 가운데쯤 "middle"로 표시.

cards.title: Starter still pulls people who need reminders.
body: Pro is $39: unlimited reminders plus bank-feed syncing. Many Starter clients chase late payments by hand. Which extra plan helps them see Pro as the clear pick?

options.text: Starter Plus at $35: Starter plus 20 reminders a month
options.feedback: This is the **decoy effect**. Starter Plus is close to Pro's price but clearly worse, so Pro looks like the obvious upgrade. Some clients will still buy Starter Plus, which is fine.

options.text: A $25 plan with 50 reminders a month
options.feedback: It may pull some clients up from Starter, but it's a genuine bargain, so some would-be Pro buyers settle for it instead.

options.text: Remove Starter so everyone starts at Pro
options.feedback: You lose price-sensitive clients entirely, and Pro becomes the cheapest plan in view instead of the smart middle.

cards.title: Same Pro plan, new neighbours.
body: Pro's price and features didn't change. What changed is what it sits next to.

breakdown.label: Business
breakdown.detail: Shown first. A real plan for firms with staff. The anchor.

breakdown.label: Pro
breakdown.detail: Unlimited reminders, bank feeds. The plan most clients need.

breakdown.label: Starter Plus
breakdown.detail: Only 20 reminders, for $4 less. The decoy.

breakdown.label: Starter
breakdown.detail: Entry plan for the very price-sensitive

cards.title: These nudges are small, and trust is big.
body: Both effects are real but modest. Business buyers who compare carefully feel them less. A fake anchor or a plan nobody should buy can look like a trick, which costs a bank more than a few sign-ups.

So keep every plan honest and useful. Then test: show the new page to half of visitors for a few weeks. Track sign-ups, but also downgrades and refunds. More Pro sign-ups that cancel in a month aren't a win.

cards.title: Now it's a freight company's quote page.
body: Shippers see two options: Economy, 7 days, $400, and Priority, 4 days, $650. Most pick Economy, though many later complain about delays.
Which third option best helps Priority?

options.feedback: **Anchoring** with a real service. Priority now sits in the middle, and urgent shippers who pick Express bring extra revenue.
A classic **decoy**: one day slower for only $20 less makes Priority look better. But you must run a service you hope nobody picks, and careful shippers may feel played.
This shifts the comparison downward. Economy becomes the middle choice, and Priority looks even pricier.

cards.softwareNote: The same page logic works for the bank's app: the anchor and the decoy are just plans instead of delivery speeds.

cards.title: Design what customers compare, not just what they pay.
body: You used two ideas. **Anchoring:** a real, higher option shown first resets what feels expensive. **The decoy effect:** a slightly worse option near your target makes the target the easy choice.
**Try it today:** open your own price list. Write down what your key offer sits next to, and ask whether that comparison helps or hurts it.
